videos.title: CoreWeave's Debt Is Cracking. AI Stocks Are Falling. So Why Is Andy Constan Watching Bond Issuance?
videos.description:
Andy Constan of Damped Spring Advisors explains why strong AI demand can coexist with financing pressure and falling stock prices. The key distinction: a difficult funding environment can hurt investors without turning into a financial crisis.

In this month’s First Principles, Andy joins Jack Forehand and Justin Carbonneau to examine CoreWeave, the commitments supporting the AI buildout, and how competition for capital affects asset prices. They also explore Treasury borrowing and buybacks, the upcoming quarterly refunding announcement, and the tension between strong earnings and ambitious expectations. Andy closes by explaining the bull case he takes seriously and why he is nevertheless positioned with some bonds and short equity exposure.

Topics covered:

- AI’s shift from cash-generating, asset-light businesses toward capital-intensive infrastructure
- CoreWeave’s funding risks and why a rising bond yield does not immediately change an existing fixed coupon
- Customer commitments, financing backstops, and the difference between stock losses and systemic contagion
- How borrowing, spending, and savings interact with the price of capital
- Why the mix of Treasury bills and longer-term bonds matters for markets
- Treasury buybacks, off-the-run bonds, and Andy Constan’s argument about interest-rate suppression
- The 20-year Treasury and possible outcomes of the quarterly refunding announcement
- Strong earnings, market breadth, and the importance of challenging your own inve

videos.title: AI Credit in Detention: Coreweave's Debt Panic & Jim Bianco's Bull Case for Bonds (Finally!)
videos.description:
This episode is brought to you by Sarmaya Partners. Learn more about Sarmaya’s LENS ETF, their full data and comparison, including performance here:
https://sarmayaetf.com/


Jim Bianco of Bianco Research called the 2022 bond bear market and stayed bearish on bonds for six years. Now, for the first time since then, he’s constructive.

Jim explains why 5% yields aren’t punishing but normal: rates should roughly track nominal GDP growth, and he expects the U.S. economy to grow at 5–6% nominally. He makes the case that inflation is stuck at 3% because the era of cheap Chinese goods is over, and explains why oil is already effectively $200 a barrel once you count tanker costs and naval security in the Strait of Hormuz. He also covers why diesel shows up in the price of everything, and why Kevin Warsh scrapping forward guidance has left markets feeling around in the dark.

On credit, Jim explains why the blowout in CCC bonds, CoreWeave included, is a handful of problem kids in detention rather than a canary in the coal mine. On AI, he argues it’s 1997, not 2000, and that the bigger risk may be that AI works.
